blocks.text: Shanghai Gave Me My Roots, Chicago Gave Me Wings
Returning to My First Hometown Through a Different Lens
Shanghai is my first hometown. Chicago is my second.

Shanghai gave me my artistic roots, my sense of beauty, and my appreciation for the subtle poetry of everyday life. Chicago gave me opportunities, freedom, and the wings to explore the world through my camera.
After many years away, I returned to Shanghai as an American, carrying with me more than two decades of experiences and a different way of seeing the world.

I spent a weekend walking its streets, photographing familiar places and unfamiliar moments. Everything felt both close and distant, familiar yet surprisingly new. I began to see Shanghai not only as the city where I grew up, but through the eyes of someone who had left, traveled far, and returned with a new perspective.

Shanghai has a special taste. It is a city to be experienced slowly, almost like savoring a cup of Chinese tea. Its beauty lives in the small details, the rhythm of everyday life, the expressions of its people, and the memories hidden in its streets.
Through my camera, I rediscovered my first hometown. I realized that distance and time had not separated me from Shanghai; they had simply taught me to appreciate it differently.
I love both cities. Shanghai is where my artistic journey began, and Chicago is where my vision grew and found its wings.
Shanghai gave me my artistic roots. Chicago gave me wings. And photography gave me the language to bring the two worlds togethe
